findings.issue: Home page re-implements the sprite resolution and card assembly that lib/cards.js:buildPokemonCards already owns, so a sprite/species bug (e.g. Deoxys) must be fixed in two places.
findings.suggestion: Extend buildPokemonCards (or add a withTypes option / separate assemble step in lib/cards.js) and have the home page consume it like the other three lists.

findings.issue: The '<count> Pokémon' + card list + empty-message block is copy-pasted verbatim in moves, abilities and types pages (and near-verbatim in the home page), so any list-wide change (sorting control, empty-state wording, pagination) is 3-4 edits.
findings.suggestion: Extract a PokemonCardList server component ({ cards, countLabel, emptyMessage }) and render it from all four pages.

findings.issue: Inline regex `/\/(\d+)\/?$/` duplicates lib/format.js:idFromUrl; behavior fixes to ID extraction won't cover this copy.
findings.suggestion: Import idFromUrl from '@/lib/format' like lib/cards.js:6 does.
Move it into lib/format.js (or lib/params.js) and import in both pages.

findings.issue: TypeBadge lives in and is exported from PokemonCard.jsx while three other modules import it, coupling them to the card module's file.
findings.suggestion: Split TypeBadge into its own component file (components/TypeBadge.jsx).

findings.issue: format.js mixes pure name/number formatting with presentation concerns (typeColorStyle inline-style builder and the SPRITE_PLACEHOLDER data-URI asset at format.js:2).
findings.suggestion: Move typeColorStyle into a styles helper and the placeholder into lib/api.js next to spriteUrlForId.

findings.issue: Column definitions are hardcoded inside MovesSection, so an Items section with similar tables must either generalize this component or copy ~90 lines of sort/aria-sort table logic.
findings.suggestion: Accept columns as a prop (key/label/numeric) so the sortable table becomes a reusable DataTable for moves, items and future tables.

summary: A well-structured App Router app: routes map to features, all API knowledge is centralized in lib/api.js, and server/client boundaries are clean, which makes removal and data-source changes easy. The main editability cost is duplication around Pokémon cards — the home page bypasses the shared card builder and the count/list/empty block is copy-pasted three times — so cross-cutting card changes need multiple edits. A small DataTable generalization and a PokemonCardList component would lift most of the remaining friction.
